headline: Permit Requirements for Alpine Recreation Areas
reservation: Daily or annual Northwest Forest Pass is required for most trailheads, while winter visitors must obtain a Sno-Park permit for plowed access points. Accommodations like the Denny Creek campground require booking months in advance via official federal systems. Verify specific seasonal pass requirements with the U.S. Forest Service before travel as regional boundaries dictate different permit types.

days.title: Waterfalls and Alpine Reflections

stops.name: Franklin Falls
stops.detail: Walk the gentle forest path to this 70-foot drop; the spray creates a lush microclimate even in mid-summer.

stops.name: Gold Creek Pond
stops.detail: Stroll the paved loop around this former gravel pit, now a serene pond reflecting the Chikamin Peak and Kendall Peak ridges.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes; conditions vary with mountain weather
days.note: Arrive early as trailhead lots frequently reach capacity by mid-morning on weekends.

days.title: High Cascade Vistas
days.start: Suggested: 7:30 AM from Snoqualmie Pass Summit

stops.name: Pacific Crest Trail - Kendall Katwalk
stops.detail: Trek a section of the famous long-distance trail to a dramatic path blasted into a sheer granite cliffside.

stops.name: Snow Lake
stops.detail: Climb through rocky switchbacks to reach the most visited alpine basin in the region, known for its deep blue water.

days.driving: Walking regional trails; allow full day for backcountry excursions
days.note: Check for lingering snow on high-altitude trails through late June.

days.title: East Slope Lakes and River History

stops.name: Kachess Lake
stops.detail: Head east to this larger reservoir for swimming and kayaking among the Ponderosa pines.

stops.name: Northwest Railway Museum
stops.detail: Visit the nearby town of Snoqualmie to explore the historic depot and learn about the rail history of the pass.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour; check I-90 pass reports for lane closures
days.note: Lake water levels fluctuate seasonally based on regional irrigation needs.

intel.title: Trailhead Congestion
intel.text: The Snow Lake and Alpental lots often fill by 8 AM during summer peak. Have a secondary plan for Gold Creek if primary areas are blocked.

intel.title: Mountain Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular service is reliable at the ski summits but fades rapidly on the PCT and toward Kachess Lake. Download offline maps at the lodge before departing.

intel.title: Pass Services
intel.text: Fuel is available at the pass summit, but prices are often higher than in North Bend or Cle Elum. Top off tanks in the valley before long mountain drives.

intel.title: Winter Travel Windows
intel.text: WSDOT frequently closes I-90 for avalanche control during heavy snow cycles. Check the official pass report for scheduled morning or evening closures.

intel.title: Permit Display
intel.text: Rangers strictly enforce the Northwest Forest Pass at federal trailheads. In winter, switch to the Sno-Park permit to avoid ticketing in plowed lots.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at BFI and stop in North Bend for groceries and a Discover Pass before the final 20-minute climb to the summit lodges.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are fine in summer, but AWD/4WD with traction tires is highly recommended for winter; check WSDOT traction laws.
plan.goldenHour: Kendall Katwalk offers expansive views for sunset, though hikers must be prepared for a descent in darkness.
